title: Electric field magnitude
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the electric field magnitude as E = (mg tanθ)/q or its simplified form (√3 mg)/(3q).

title: Electric field direction
description: Essential: States the electric field direction is horizontal and to the right (or opposite the electric force on the positive charge).

title: Speed at lowest point
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the speed at point C using energy conservation, resulting in v = √[2gL(1 - √3/3)] or equivalent.

title: Tension at lowest point
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the tension at point C using Newton's second law for circular motion, resulting in T = 3mg - (2√3/3)mg or equivalent.

title: Force equilibrium setup
description: Important: Applies force balance (horizontal and vertical) at the initial equilibrium point A to relate electric force, tension, and weight.

title: Energy conservation setup
description: Important: Correctly applies the work-energy theorem between points B and C, accounting for work done by both gravity and the electric field.

title: Centripetal force setup
description: Important: Applies Newton's second law at point C, identifying the net force (T - mg) as the centripetal force.

title: Sign error in work
description: Pitfall: Uses incorrect sign for the work done by the electric field in the energy equation (e.g., adds instead of subtracts).

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Maintains consistent units throughout the solution or explicitly includes them in final answers.
